objective: metric round 6, with HBAA +0.701 as the bar

metrics.title: Hyperbolic temperatured expected rank of the true target's level-1 cell, chance-normalised by an analytic size-matched null.
metrics.formula:
Poincare ball B_1^d, curvature c = 1 (radius 1). Poincare distance d(x,y) = 2 * artanh( || (-x) (+) y || ), with (+) the Mobius addition.
  Reference: frozen source point s_i and target point t_i in B_1^d for every item i (N items).
  1. For each level-1 code k in {1..K}: I_k = the items whose level-1 code is k; nu_k = Karcher (Frechet) barycentre in B_1^d of { t_i : i in I_k }, computed by the fixed iteration nu <- exp_nu( (1/|I_k|) * sum_{i in I_k} log_nu(t_i) ), exactly 10 iterations, initialised at the target point of the smallest-index member of I_k.
  2. Query point of item i: v_i = (1/|H_i|) * sum_{j in H_i} log_0(s_j) in the tangent space at the origin; q_i = exp_0(v_i), where H_i is the training-split history of item i. If the reference exposes only one source vector per item, H_i = {i} and q_i = s_i.
  3. D_ik = d(q_i, nu_k).
  4. tau = median over i of d(q_i, t_i). One scalar computed once from the reference and the training split; identical for all 97 tables, never recomputed per table.
  5. p_i(k) = exp(-D_ik/tau) / sum_{k'=1..K} exp(-D_ik'/tau).
  6. r_i(k) = 1 + #{ k' : D_ik' < D_ik } + 0.5 * #{ k' != k : D_ik' = D_ik }.
  7. Rbar = (1/N) * sum_{i=1..N} sum_{k=1..K} p_i(k) * r_i(k).
  8. HERC = 1 - (Rbar - 1) / ((K - 1)/2) for K >= 2; HERC = 0 if K = 1.
  Higher is better. The denominator (K-1)/2 equals ((K+1)/2 - 1), the exact expected rank of a uniformly random code assignment, so a chance table scores 0 at every K.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table's level-1 integer code per item; the frozen Issue #126 reference arrays s_i and t_i (learned on training pairs only); the training split (to form H_i). Nothing else.
metrics.geometry: curvature -1, c = 1. It enters three times. The prototypes nu_k are Frechet barycentres inside the ball, produced by an exp/log gradient iteration, not an arithmetic mean. The query is a tangent-space barycentre at the origin pushed back by exp_0, so its magnitude is a hyperbolic radius, not a Euclidean norm. Every D_ik is a Poincare distance whose conformal factor shrinks the metric near the boundary, so moving a prototype from radius 0.5 to 0.95 costs far more than 0.45 Euclidean units. Ranks and the tau-normalised softmax use only these curved distances.
metrics.why: Recall@10 needs the ground-truth target's level-1 cell to be among the cells a query can reach. HERC scores exactly that cell's expected rank, under a softmax over all K cells rather than over the mean of ten sampled negatives. Three things are new relative to HBAA and Q_H. (a) The positive is a target-side Frechet barycentre, i.e. the whole semantic cell, not one anchor's point, so a cell that is right on average is rewarded even when its anchor happens to be off. (b) The negative side is the full cell distribution through a temperatured expected rank, so a cell that is merely second-best everywhere still loses ground, which a mean margin over ten negatives cannot detect. (c) Dividing by the analytic random-assignment rank (K-1)/2 makes the number immune to the level-1 bucket count: this is the size-matched null whose absence drove the plain path likelihood to -0.49 on collapsed tables. The tau normalisation additionally makes the statistic invariant to radial rescaling of the reference, which destabilised the covering-radius and margin statistics.
metrics.compute: N = 24587 queries x K <= 256 prototypes = 6.3M Poincare distances, vectorisable in numpy (~50 MB, 10-20 s); K Karcher means cost 10 passes over 24587 points each (~2 s); log/exp maps are elementwise. Well under one minute, no fitting, no Stage 2 or Stage 3 run.
metrics.risks: if tau is much larger than the spread of D_ik the softmax flattens to uniform and every table tends to 0, losing discrimination. Large cells dominate the barycentres, so a table good only for hub items can score moderately. Near-duplicate nu_k create rank ties and the 0.5 tie-break biases toward chance. K = 2 gives a coarse three-level score and a wide confidence interval.
metrics.failure_mode: worst on the radially degenerate table whose level-1 codes are random but geometrically centred: every nu_k collapses to the same point near the origin, all D_ik are equal, p is uniform, Rbar = (K+1)/2, so HERC = 0. A one-code table is 0 by definition. A table whose cells are cleanly separated but semantically wrong (high bucket count, tidy Voronoi geometry) also scores at or below 0, which is exactly where bucket count and covering radius were fooled.

metrics.title: Horospherical lift of level-1 bucket barycentres against the history's boundary direction, standardised over all buckets.
metrics.formula: Fix curvature c=1 (K=-1). Work in the Poincare ball B^d={x in R^d: ||x||<1} with d_B(x,y)=arcosh(1+2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). Let b(i) in {1..K} be the level-1 integer code of item i, N=24587. Let x_i in B^d be the frozen reference SOURCE representation of item i. For a finite set S, let bar(S)=argmin_{m in B^d} sum_{j in S} d_B(m,x_j)^2, computed by Karcher iteration m <- exp_m((1/|S|) sum_j log_m(x_j)), 10 steps, initialised at the Euclidean mean rescaled to norm 0.9; log/exp are the Poincare ball maps. For each training history h (an item sequence) with next item i+(h): u_h = bar({x_j : j in h}); xi_h = u_h/||u_h|| in boundary S^{d-1} (skip h if ||u_h||<1e-6). Busemann function at boundary point xi: b_xi(x) = log( (1-||x||^2) / ||x-xi||^2 ) (curvature -1; for curvature -c divide by 2*sqrt(c) and replace x by sqrt(c)x). For each level-1 bucket k=1..K let m_k = bar({x_i : b(i)=k}). For each h compute y_k(h)=b_{xi_h}(m_k), then z_k(h)=(y_k(h)-mean_{k'} y_{k'}(h))/(std_{k'} y_{k'}(h)+1e-12). The metric is M = (1/|H|) sum_{h in H} tanh( z_{b(i+(h))}(h) ). H is a deterministic subset of the training histories of size min(|H_train|, 2048), selected by the 2048 smallest 64-bit hashes of the history's item-id tuple. Constants: c=1 (fixed negative curvature), 10 Karcher steps, 2048=2^11 <= N/12 (a fixed compute cap, not tuned), 1e-12 numerical floor; no parameter is fitted to the 97 recalls.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table's level-1 integer code per item; (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference's per-item SOURCE representation x_i (training-pairs-only model, no target side, no interaction scores); (3) the TRAINING split histories and their next items. Nothing else: no validation pair, no test pair, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: Curvature enters twice. (a) The Karcher barycentre bar(.) is the Frechet mean in the fixed-curvature -1 Poincare ball; its position, not a Euclidean average, defines both the bucket point m_k and the history direction xi_h. (b) The scoring function is the Busemann function of a horosphere, b_xi(x)=log((1-||x||^2)/||x-xi||^2). Horospheres and Busemann functions are a purely negatively-curved object: they are the level sets of the asymptotic "height" toward a boundary point, and the formula uses the Poincare ball's conformal factor. In Euclidean space the same expression has no horosphere meaning, and b_xi is not a distance; it linearises the Gromov product only because of negative curvature. Thus the comparison of a bucket's hyperbolic position against the history's boundary direction is meaningful only through the map.
metrics.why: For each training history, the frozen reference places the true next item in a particular region of the ball; Stage-3 recall is high when the SID table's level-1 bucket occupies that same region, because beam search then spends its level-1 branch on the right subtree. HBAA measures this with the finite Gromov product (u_h | m_b), i.e. proximity to the history point, and with a mean over ten sampled negatives. This metric instead projects every bucket barycentre onto the horosphere foliation centred at the history's asymptotic direction xi_h and asks whether the true bucket is higher than the table's other buckets, standardised over ALL K-1 negative buckets. It therefore (i) uses the whole bucket through its hyperbolic barycentre, not just a bucket label, (ii) uses the full negative distribution over buckets rather than ten negatives, which removes negative-sampling variance, and (iii) separates "depth toward the predicted future" (Busemann height) from "nearness to the observed history point" (Gromov product): two tables can have the same Gromov alignment yet different horospherical ordering, and the latter is what the beam search consumes. Because z is standardised within each history and the metric is a mean of tanh, a collapsed table (K=1, or all bucket barycentres on one horosphere) returns exactly 0, matching the observed collapse failure of plain path likelihood.
metrics.compute: K<=256 buckets, d is the reference dimension (order 64), |H|<=2048, N=24587. The bucket barycentres m_k are computed once: O(K*N*d*10) in the worst case but only over items, about 4e7 float ops. Each history needs one Karcher mean over its own short sequence and K Busemann evaluations of K*d dot products: 2048*256*64 ~ 3.4e7 float ops. Total well under one minute, no N-by-N matrix and no per-pair Stage-2/3 work.
metrics.risks: If x_i cluster near the origin, every ||u_h|| is small, xi_h is unstable and b_xi is nearly flat, so z is noise; the 1e-6 and 1e-12 floors only avoid division by zero. If a table has very few buckets, std_k y_k is small and z is volatile; tanh bounds the damage but does not remove it. If the reference's source ball uses a different curvature or scaling than c=1, the Busemann values are rescaled (monotone per history, so z is invariant) but the Karcher means are not; the reference's own curvature must be used as c if it is not 1. Histories longer than the training window are truncated exactly as in the training split. A table that assigns codes by item frequency rather than semantics can still produce nonzero z by chance; the mean over 2048 histories makes this small but not exactly zero.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on a one-code table (K=1: z is 0 by construction, M=0), on a uniformly random relabelling of the codes (E[M]=0), and on any table whose level-1 buckets all have the same Busemann height at the histories' directions (all m_k on a common horosphere, e.g. all bucket barycentres at the origin, giving std_k y_k ~0 and M~0). It is also weak on a table with two enormous buckets split by a direction orthogonal to every xi_h.

metrics.title: Cross-tower hyperbolic soft rank of the true level-1 bucket among all codebook buckets
metrics.formula: Let N=24587 items, V=256 level-1 codes, c(i) the level-1 code of item i, n_b=#{i: c(i)=b}, V_eff=#{b: n_b>0}. Let x_i (source rep) and y_i (target rep) be the frozen reference arrays. Set s = 0.9 / Q99_i max(||x_i||,||y_i||) and curvature c = 1. For the Poincare ball B_c^d write exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v / (sqrt(c)||v||) (exp_0^c(0)=0), log_0^c(z) = (1/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||z||) z/||z|| (log_0^c(0)=0), d_B(z,z') = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||(-z) (+) z'||), with (+) the Mobius sum. Write E(v)=exp_0^c(s v). For a finite set Z in the ball let F(Z)=argmin_m sum_{z in Z} d_B(m,z)^2 be the Frechet (Karcher) barycentre, computed from m0=exp_0^c(mean_{z in Z} log_0^c z) by m <- exp_m^c(mean_{z in Z} log_m^c z) until the step norm < 1e-6 or 50 iterations. For every nonempty bucket b define Z_b={E(y_j): c(j)=b}, m_b=F(Z_b), rho_b=(1/n_b) sum_{j:c(j)=b} d_B(0,E(y_j)), and the radially corrected centroid mtil_b = exp_0^c( (rho_b/d_B(0,m_b)) log_0^c(m_b) ) if m_b != 0, else 0. Let T be the training interactions deduplicated to one per target item (keep its LAST occurrence in the training split), and for t in T let i(t) be the target item and h(t) its training history. Define q_t = exp_0^c( (1/|h(t)|) sum_{j in h(t)} log_0^c(E(x_j)) ). Derive the temperature tau = median_{t in T} d_B(q_t, E(y_{i(t)})). For each t let b_t=c(i(t)), d_+(t)=d_B(q_t, mtil_{b_t}), and d_b(t)=d_B(q_t, mtil_b). Define P_t = (1/(V_eff-1)) sum_{b != b_t, n_b>0} sigma((d_b(t)-d_+(t))/tau), with sigma(z)=1/(1+exp(-z)); if V_eff=1 set P_t=1/2. The metric is H = (1/|T|) sum_{t in T} (2 P_t - 1), a scalar in [-1,+1], higher is better.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported Stage-2 SID table, i.e. the integer code per item per level (only the level-1 column is read); (2) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference arrays x_i (source) and y_i (target) for i=1..N, learned on training pairs only; (3) the TRAINING split, used only to build T and the histories h(t). Nothing else; no validation or test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: the whole computation lives in the Poincare ball of unit negative curvature c=1 after the reference-derived scale s. Curvature enters in four places: the exp_0/log_0 maps that place the reference vectors and define the history query, the Frechet/Karcher barycentres m_b, the geodesic radial renormalisation mtil_b (which moves the centroid out along its own geodesic ray to the mean member radius), and the hyperbolic distance d_B inside the logistic soft rank. At c -> 0 the same expression collapses to a Euclidean centroid plus Euclidean distance, so the curvature is not decorative; the artanh nonlinearity and the barycentre corrections change which bucket is ranked first.
metrics.why: Stage-3 recall@10 is decided first at level 1: if the true item's level-1 region is not closer to the history query than the other ~255 regions, no deeper decoding can recover the item. P_t is exactly a soft, temperature-smoothed Recall@1-over-buckets computed with the reference's own geometry, and H is its centred average, so it is a direct proxy for whether the table's coarse routing is aligned with the reference's query-to-candidate metric. Over Q_H it adds the full V-way negative distribution (every other bucket centroid, not a prefix count or a margin against one reference), the target tower (the side a query is actually matched against, while the query is built from the source tower), geodesic barycentres, and a size-unbiased radial correction. Over HBAA it adds a nonlinear soft rank over the whole bucket distribution instead of a linear inner-product margin against a mean of ten negatives: one hard negative cannot be averaged away, and the temperature comes from the reference's own positive query-target distance, so no recall-tuned constant exists. Under a uniformly random relabelling P_t has expectation exactly 1/2 by the symmetry sigma(z)+sigma(-z)=1, and under a one-code table V_eff=1 forces P_t=1/2, so both controls map to 0 and collapse is never rewarded.
metrics.compute: build at most 256 Karcher barycentres over all N=24587 target vectors (O(N d * iterations), ~3e7 scalar ops for d=128); build at most N=24587 history queries with the closed-form tangent mean (O(|T| H d), with H the mean history length); evaluate |T|*V_eff <= 24587*256 = 6.3e6 hyperbolic distances by vectorised matrix operations. The radial corrections and logistic ranks are O(N + |T| V). Total is a few seconds on CPU and well under one minute, with no pairwise N x N matrix.
metrics.risks: If the reference's target arrays are not the query-side/candidate embeddings but something else, the cross-tower distance is meaningless and P_t sits at 1/2 for every table. If the target vectors are nearly isotropic and low-rank so that all bucket centroids are almost equidistant from every query, P_t is near 1/2 for all 97 tables and the metric cannot discriminate. The radial renormalisation removes the Poincare contraction bias of large buckets but also discards any genuine magnitude/confidence signal, which could lower the correlation. Tables with very few nonempty level-1 codes give a coarse, high-variance P_t; a 2-code but informative split can score high even though it cannot isolate a top-10 item set. Using only the last training occurrence per target item samples a particular query distribution; a different but still training-only deduplication would change the value, though not the form. Near-boundary vectors make artanh and the Karcher iteration stiff; the 0.9 scaling keeps every mapped point strictly inside the ball.
metrics.failure_mode: the worst table is a level-1 partition anti-aligned with the reference's target-tower geometry, e.g. codes assigned to maximise target-space dispersion within a bucket or to invert the reference's neighbourhoods; then d_+ is larger than almost every d_b, P_t -> 0 and H -> -1. The degenerate table that must be worst for usefulness, the one-code collapse, gives V_eff=1, hence P_t=1/2 and H=0 (not rewarded rather than punished). A uniformly random or hash-based relabelling gives H approximately 0, and a table whose level-1 buckets are balanced but semantically empty also lands near 0.

metrics.title: Level-1 SID cells scored by their tempered hyperbolic expected-rank gained over the exact cell-size prior, with every training query of the history voting and cell centroids at source-target geodesic midpoints.
metrics.formula:
Poincare ball B = {x in R^d : ||x|| < 1} with constant sectional curvature -1. Distance d(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))); exp_x and log_x are the Riemannian exponential and logarithm of B. Item i has frozen source and target representations u_i, v_i in B. Define the item's canonical point a_i = exp_{u_i}( (1/2) * log_{u_i}(v_i) ), the geodesic midpoint of u_i and v_i (fraction 1/2 is the canonical midpoint, not a fitted weight). The table assigns code_1(i) in {1..K}; n_k = #{j : code_1(j) = k}; N = 24587. Cell centroid c_k = argmin_{c in B} sum_{j: code_1(j)=k} d(c, a_j)^2, computed by 50 fixed iterations c <- exp_c( (1/n_k) * sum_j log_c(a_j) ) from the Euclidean mean of the a_j projected into B. Tr = the training split's ordered pairs (i, g) (source item i, gold target item g, both present in the table). tau = the frozen reference temperature, used exactly as the reference uses it, i.e. the reference's score for a candidate x given query q is -d(q,x)/tau. Set k*(i) = code_1(g) for the pair (i,g). For every pair:
  ER_prior(i) = 1 + sum_{k != k*(i)} n_k / (n_k + n_{k*(i)})        [the exact untempered log-prior rank of the gold cell: sigma(log n_k - log n_{k*}) = n_k/(n_k+n_{k*})]
  ER_geo(i)   = 1 + sum_{k != k*(i)} sigma( ( d(u_i, c_k) - d(u_i, c_{k*(i)}) ) / tau ),  sigma(z) = 1/(1+exp(-z))
  M = (1/|Tr|) * sum_{(i,g) in Tr} ( ER_prior(i) - ER_geo(i) ) / K,   and M = 0 when K = 1.
M is one scalar, in [-1, +1], higher is better. It equals the fraction of the K cells whose expected placement the cell geometry resolves beyond what the cells' sizes already resolve.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported Stage-2 SID table: item id -> level-1 integer code; (2) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference: per-item source representation u_i and target representation v_i in the ball, plus its temperature tau; (3) the training split's (source item, target item) pairs. Nothing else: no level-2/3/4 codes, no validation pair, no test pair, no recall value.
metrics.geometry: curvature -1 enters three times and is load-bearing in each. (i) The comparison between the query and a cell is the Poincare distance d, whose arcosh of the conformal-factor ratio is not a Euclidean distance and cannot be obtained by rescaling one. (ii) Each cell is a genuine Frechet (Karcher) barycentre in the ball, obtained by 50 iterations of the exponential of the mean of tangent logs - an operation with no flat analogue because it depends on the basepoint. (iii) Each item's canonical point is the geodesic midpoint exp_u(log_u(v)/2), so the target half of the reference is transported into the source chart along the geodesic, which again is only defined by the exp/log pair. The curvature is not introduced as a rescaling of a Euclidean score: d appears inside a logistic whose argument is a difference of geodesic distances to the gold centroid, so cells at different radii are treated differently than their Euclidean separation would imply.
metrics.why: Stage 3 generates candidates through the level-1 prefix and reranks, so recall@10 is governed by one question per query: does the cell holding the true item beat every other cell, under the reference geometry, by more than popularity would already predict. Q_H answers a coarser version (a single prefix ranking score) and HBAA answers a narrower one (one global history barycentre contrasted against the mean of ten negatives through a Gromov inner product). This metric adds three things none of the measured ones has. First, the whole training history enters as a distribution of queries - every training source is its own query point - instead of being collapsed into one barycentre; a table can be good on average and bad for the particular sources Stage 3 will see, and only per-query voting sees that. Second, the negative side is the full tempered distribution over all K cells (an expected rank), not a mean over ten negatives, so a table that leaves a single competing cell close to the true cell is penalised in proportion to the recall it loses, and that penalty is invisible to a mean. Third, the cell centroids are built from the source-target geodesic midpoints, i.e. from the target half of the frozen reference, which every measured metric leaves unused; a prefix that clusters items by what they are, as reachable from their sources, is what makes the prefix a usable candidate filter. The subtraction of the exact size prior is what makes this a quality measure rather than a popularity measure: a cell whose centroid merely sits near the global mean because it is huge gains nothing, so the number cannot be bought by collapsing buckets, and the query-to-target geometry must actually separate the gold cell from all others.
metrics.compute: one pass over 24587 items to build the a_i (24587 exp/log pairs), 50 Karcher sweeps over the same 24587 vectors in total (each item belongs to exactly one cell), then one |Tr| x K matrix of geodesic distances to the centroids and two |Tr| x K logistic reductions; with K <= 256 and |Tr| on the order of the item count this is about 6e6 distance evaluations, a few seconds in vectorised numpy, well under a minute per table, and the a_i and centroids depend only on the table and the reference so they are reused unchanged for the other 96 tables.
metrics.risks: (1) If tau is large relative to the spread of the geodesic distances, every ER_geo tends to (K+1)/2 regardless of the table and M degenerates into mean(ER_prior) - (K+1)/2 divided by K, i.e. a pure cell-size statistic; if tau is very small the logistic saturates and M becomes a hard rank driven by a handful of near-tied cells and becomes noisy. (2) The construction needs u_i and v_i in the same ball; if the reference stores targets in a different chart or applies a relation transform outside B, the midpoint is undefined and only a relation-corrected substitute would work. (3) Cell sizes are typically skewed, so pairs whose gold cell is tiny contribute ER_prior near K and dominate the mean; M then tracks performance on the rare-cell subset rather than the average, and its variance across the 97 tables is inflated. (4) If the training sources all have nearly the same representation the per-query voting collapses back to a single global query and the metric loses its advantage over HBAA. (5) A coarse table (K = 2..4) whose two or three cells happen to be geometrically clean reaches 0.5-0.75 and is over-rewarded relative to a fine, moderately good table, because the gain is bounded by K-1 while the divisor is only K.
metrics.failure_mode: the worst table is the one whose level-1 codes are essentially item-identifying, K close to N with one or two items per code. Then each centroid c_k is the cell's own item midpoint, the cell-level ranking reproduces the reference's own item-level ranking, the size prior is uniform (all n_k = 1 gives ER_prior = (K+1)/2) and M saturates at approximately +0.5 for every such table independently of its content - the number stops discriminating at exactly the regime where the level-1 prefix degenerates into an item id, the same pathology that costs Q_H its Spearman at levels 2 and 3. It is worst in the other direction on a table whose cells split by popularity rather than semantics: the size prior already ranks the gold cell first, ER_prior is near 1, and M is driven to -1 even though the cells are internally coherent.
